unit.why: A naming segulah attributed to the Vilna Gaon, proved by a brief anecdote: his daughter's children kept dying, and the child named by his instruction lived. Neither the figure nor the setting is Hasidic.
unit.boundary_note: The final words 'סגולה לחולי הידוע ר״ל' are the heading of the next item (ד) and belong to the next division.

stories.start_quote: עוד יש סגולה לזה מאת הגר״א
stories.summary_en: The Vilna Gaon's remedy for parents whose children die is to give the next child the name of the last deceased sibling, with a new name added first; his daughter, whose children had died, did this, and that child and her later children lived.

tags.why: The anecdote is wrapped in a segulah or customs discussion and serves as its proof.

quotes: סגולה זאת בדוקה הוא כי כן היה מעשה בבת הגר״א
tags.why: It attests the efficacy of a non-Hasidic sage's advice.

quotes: כי כן היה מעשה בבת הגר״א
tags.why: The Gaon's daughter is the protagonist.

quotes: וכאשר הולידה בן מחדש עשתה כדברי הגר״א
tags.why: The daughter is the central actor and carries out the remedy.
The deaths of her children set up the story.
The birth of the new son is the event the remedy acts on.

quotes: וחי הילד וגם הילדים אשר ילדה אח״כ חיו
tags.why: The child's survival is presented as the segulah's supernatural effect.

quotes: יקראהו בשם אחיו אשר מת לפניו באחרונה
tags.why: The sage's instruction averts the expected death of the child, though no tsaddik intervenes directly.

missing_concepts: naming custom / changing or adding a name to avert death
